svg.title: Reader + overlay side panel — medium portrait — light (Notes tab)
svg.desc: Reader on a portrait tablet, medium (600–839dp), light theme, touch density. Side panel as a 360dp overlay sheet with scrim (PDF does not resize). Notes tab: synced, device-local, waiting-to-sync and editing NoteCards; composer.

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: 3.2 Attention

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: An attention function can be described as mapping a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output, where

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: the query, keys, values, and output are all vectors. The output is computed as a weighted sum of the values,

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: where the weight assigned to each value is computed by a compatibility function of the query with the

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: corresponding key.

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: 3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: We call our particular attention "Scaled Dot-Product Attention" (Figure 2). The input consists of queries and

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: keys of dimension dk, and values of dimension dv. We compute the dot products of the query with all keys,

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: divide each by √dk, and apply a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values.

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: In practice, we compute the attention function on a set of queries simultaneously, packed together into a

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: matrix Q. The keys and values are also packed together into matrices K and V. We compute the matrix of

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: outputs as:

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / √dk) V (1)

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: The two most commonly used attention functions are additive attention [2], and dot-product (multiplicative)

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: attention. Dot-product attention is identical to our algorithm, except for the scaling factor of 1/√dk. Additive

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: attention computes the compatibility function using a feed-forward network with a single hidden layer. While

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: the two are similar in theoretical complexity, dot-product attention is much faster and more space-efficient in

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: practice, since it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code.

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: While for small values of dk the two mechanisms perform similarly, additive attention outperforms dot

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: product attention without scaling for larger values of dk [3]. We suspect that for large values of dk, the dot

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: gradients. To counteract this effect, we scale the dot products by 1/√dk.

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: 3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: Instead of performing a single attention function with dmodel-dimensional keys, values and queries, we found

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: it beneficial to linearly project the queries, keys and values h times with different, learned linear projections to

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: dk, dk and dv dimensions, respectively. On each of these projected versions of queries, keys and values we

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: then perform the attention function in parallel, yielding dv-dimensional output values. These are concatenated

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: and once again projected, resulting in the final values.

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: at different positions. With a single attention head, averaging inhibits this.

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat(head1, ..., headh) W^O (2)

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: In this work we employ h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads. For each of these we use dk = dv = dmodel/h

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: = 64. Due to the reduced dimension of each head, the total computational cost is similar to that of

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: single-head attention with full dimensionality.

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: 3.3 Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: In addition to attention sub-layers, each of the layers in our encoder and decoder contains a fully connected

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: feed-forward network, which is applied to each position separately and identically. This consists of two linear

text.font-family: Geist, 'Segoe UI', 'SF Pro Text', Roboto, sans-serif

svg.text: transformations with a ReLU activation in between.
